description: EV model uses full-data fit for all deliveries including WP-training matches. The comment at line 143-150 explicitly notes 'cross-fitting is the production version' but uses full_ev instead. This means a player's own performances contribute to their own expected-performance baseline — in-sample bias. The identity-free property claimed in the methodology is violated for WP-training matches.
impact_on_rankings: Moderate: biases v_bat/v_bowl for players with many deliveries in WP-training matches; could lift or depress individual ratings by an estimated 2-5 R-units for the most exposed players
proposed_fix: Implement leave-one-match-out cross-fitting: for each match, refit the EV model on all other matches and score that match's deliveries with the held-out model. Code skeleton already exists in step2 comments.

description: Win-probability model uses a single engineered feature per innings (proj_margin for inn1 based on runs_before + E_remaining - venue_par; runs_advantage for inn2 based on E_remaining - runs_required_before). Severely underspecified — cannot distinguish 'teams tied on a flat pitch' from 'teams tied on a turning track in final over'. Brier score = 0.1925 is marginal; tail calibration fails badly.
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: leverage L(s) is computed from |WP_after - WP_before| using miscalibrated probabilities. At decile 0 the model predicts 4.3% win probability but actual win rate is 9.5% — a 118% overstatement of losing probability. This systematically mis-ranks extreme-state deliveries and therefore distorts PI for the highest-pressure situations
proposed_fix: Add wickets_before explicitly as a direct feature (independent of E_remaining). Consider current run rate vs par run rate. Add match-phase indicator (powerplay/middle/death). Apply isotonic regression or Platt scaling post-hoc to fix tail calibration.

description: Empirical WP calibration shows significant miscalibration at both tails. Decile 0: predicted mean WP = 0.043 vs actual win rate = 0.095 (overestimates losing probability by 2.2x). Decile 1: predicted 0.150 vs actual 0.111. Decile 7: predicted 0.747 vs actual 0.816. Calibration is acceptable only in the middle deciles (4-6).
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: Leverage = sum_outcomes P(outcome|state) × |WP_after - WP_before|. Tail miscalibration means leverage in extreme match states (team nearly beaten or nearly won) is systematically wrong — these are precisely the highest-PI deliveries. Players who performed well in extreme-state situations may be incorrectly rated.
proposed_fix: Apply isotonic calibration or Platt scaling to WP model outputs before computing leverage. Re-evaluate calibration by competition class separately (IPL vs T20I).

description: Resource monotonicity checks V2_resource_mono_balls and V2_resource_mono_wkts both FAIL. The expected-remaining-runs table c(s) is non-monotone in both balls-remaining and wickets-lost dimensions. A wicket in certain states appears to cost more runs remaining than the adjacent state
proposed_fix: MEDIUM: Affects v_bat/v_bowl anomalies for deliveries in non-monotone states. Death-over batters and tailenders are most exposed because c(s) is most volatile in low-ball high-wicket states. Direction of bias is non-obvious — could lift or depress specific players depending on which states are non-monotone.
effort: Apply isotonic regression constraint along the wickets dimension for each balls_left_bin. Enforce that c(s) weakly decreases as balls_left decreases (fewer balls = fewer expected runs). Rerun step2 and validate.

description: PI is computed as within-competition percentile rank of leverage: PI_t = legal_press['leverage'].rank(pct=True) within each competition class. This guarantees PI is exactly uniform U(0,1) by construction. Consequence: PI = 0.80 is always the top-20% threshold regardless of actual leverage magnitude. A T20I final with extreme leverage and an IPL group match with mild variance are treated on the same percentile scale — cross-format PI values are not comparable in absolute leverage terms.
impact_on_rankings: MEDIUM: Does not invalidate within-format rankings but means the HP threshold (PI >= 0.80) captures exactly 20% of deliveries by definition regardless of competition. Players who happen to have more deliveries in genuinely high-leverage competitions are not rewarded for it.
proposed_fix: Report absolute leverage L(s) alongside percentile PI. Consider using a competition-pooled leverage threshold (e.g. L(s) > median IPL leverage) rather than independent within-competition percentiles.

description: The model measures value-added above context-adjusted expected performance weighted by leverage percentile. This is NOT the same as 'performance under pressure' in a psychological or situational sense. Leverage measures win-probability sensitivity to outcomes — a mechanistic property of the game state. It does not capture batter/bowler psychological state or fielding context. The methodology should disclose this distinction more prominently.
impact_on_rankings: LOW: Does not change rankings but affects how they are communicated and defended. A reviewer may challenge whether leverage is a valid proxy for pressure exposure.
proposed_fix: Add explicit disclosure in technical report: 'Pressure is operationalised as match-state leverage (win-probability sensitivity), not as psychological pressure. Leverage is a necessary but not sufficient condition for psychological pressure.' Cite supporting literature.

description: Shrinkage formula uses n_reg (regular-match delivery count) for the precision weight: n = max(row['n_reg'], 1) at line 246. A T20I specialist with 200 T20I deliveries and 20 IPL deliveries has n_reg = 20 → heavily shrunk despite substantial total pressure exposure. This systematically disadvantages T20I specialists relative to IPL-heavy players of equivalent true ability.
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: T20I specialists (e.g. Zaman Khan with 200 T20I deliveries and 0 IPL) are shrunk more than IPL players with comparable n_hp. The ranking differences are hard to quantify without rerunning with n_total substituted for n_reg, but the effect is real and directional.
proposed_fix: For the shrinkage step use n_total_press (total HP deliveries across all formats) rather than n_reg. Alternatively use n_total. The current choice was not documented in the methodology approval records as an explicit decision.

description: Potential ambiguity in KO adjustment: R_overall = R_reg + w_K × (kappa + delta_i) × 100. R_reg is computed from reg_cats = ['IPL league', 'T20I non-knockout']. KO deliveries are excluded from R_reg. So there is NO double-counting. However: the pressure slope theta_i (which modulates R_reg) is estimated from n_reg only (line 246). If a player's true theta_i is better estimated from their KO-match data, the slope is noisier for KO-heavy players. Additionally w_K = 0.0529 is a leverage-share proportion — not a performance-impact or importance weight derived from player data.
impact_on_rankings: LOW for double-counting (confirmed not present). MEDIUM for theta estimation: KO-heavy players with fewer regular matches have noisier slope estimates which then feed into R_reg, indirectly affecting R_overall.
proposed_fix: Document the w_K derivation explicitly. Add sensitivity check: compare R_overall with w_K set to 0.0 and 0.10. Estimate theta from all matches not just regular ones.

description: 3 out of 10 bowler 90% CIs include zero: Shakib Al Hasan [-0.382 to 63.510], Wayne Parnell [-8.420 to 73.095], Akash Madhwal [-28.894 to 82.298]. These players' ratings are not statistically distinguishable from zero (no pressure performance effect). Prabhsimran Singh CI also barely excludes zero [-0.198 to 57.617]. In any standard frequentist framework these players would not be declared to have a positive pressure performance signal.
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: Shakib Al Hasan (rank 9), Wayne Parnell (rank 6), Akash Madhwal (rank 10) cannot be reliably distinguished from zero effect. Including them in a 'top 10' without prominent disclaimers overstates evidence. The bootstrap CI half-widths for Madhwal (55.6 R-units) are extreme.
proposed_fix: Add mandatory CI disclosure for all ranked players. Apply more conservative eligibility: require that 90% bootstrap CI excludes zero as an additional gate, or at minimum flag such players with an asterisk and disclaimer.

description: Corbin Bosch (rank 1 bowler) has n_hp = 99 and n_hp_matches = 8. Under the n_hp >= 100 'sustained performer' threshold he is INELIGIBLE. Under the approved n_hp >= 50 and matches >= 5 threshold he is eligible with n_hp = 99 (one delivery short of 100). His ranking is therefore threshold-sensitive: the difference of one delivery determines his eligibility at the stronger threshold.
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: If the presentation or evaluator applies the 100-delivery standard, Bosch is excluded. Additionally his bootstrap SE (22.1) is substantially larger than analytical SE (16.7) indicating match-level clustering. With only 8 pressure matches this is expected but means his CI is wide.
proposed_fix: Flag Bosch as a threshold-boundary case. Report alongside the n_hp>=100 leaderboard where he does not appear. Explain the threshold choice explicitly in the presentation.

description: In step2_expected_value.py line 205, the non_striker_runout flag uses dismissal_type == 'Run Out' (with space). The actual data uses 'RunOut' (no space). Therefore the step2 non_striker_runout column is always 0. However this column is NOT used in step4 — step4 independently re-identifies runout dismissals from the pressure CSV using the corrected string 'RunOut'. So the net effect on v_bat/v_bowl computation is zero.
impact_on_rankings: ZERO net impact: step4 RunOut handling is correct. step2 column is populated incorrectly but not used in production ranking computation.
proposed_fix: Fix the string in step2 for consistency and documentation completeness. The step4 fix is correct and sufficient.

description: compute_role_params() uses min_n=60 (deliveries in regular matches) to estimate league-wide role parameters. But eligibility requires n_total >= 120 (or n_hp >= 50). Role priors are therefore estimated from a potentially different (and smaller) set of players than the eligible pool. This is not a large bias but it is an internal inconsistency.
impact_on_rankings: LOW: Role priors (mu_prior, sigma_signal) are population-level hyperparameters. Slight difference in the estimation set has second-order effects on individual ratings.
proposed_fix: Align min_n for role-prior computation with the eligibility threshold. Use n_total >= 50 (or n_hp >= 50) as the population filter consistently.

description: P(top10) is computed via Monte Carlo simulation from summary statistics (mu_i, se_boot) rather than from actual per-draw bootstrap rankings. This means the reported P(top10) assumes a Gaussian distribution of ratings which may not hold (particularly for players near the threshold or with skewed bootstrap distributions).
impact_on_rankings: MEDIUM: P(top10) is used for ranking robustness assessment. If the bootstrap distribution is skewed, Gaussian-based P(top10) over- or under-states inclusion probability. This is most consequential for borderline players (ranks 8-12).
proposed_fix: Store per-draw rankings from bootstrap and compute P(top10) empirically. With 500 resamples this is straightforward and would validate the Gaussian approximation.

description: Free-hit deliveries use the same EV baseline as normal deliveries despite the fundamental rule difference: a batter cannot be dismissed (except run out) on a free hit. Expected wicket probability should be near zero on free hits, so the c(s) × E[wicket] component of EV overstates the value of a wicket for the BOWLER and understates the advantage to the BATTER on free hits.
impact_on_rankings: LOW: Free hits are a small fraction of total deliveries (~2%). The error is directional: bowlers slightly over-penalised, batters slightly under-rewarded on free hits. Impact on rankings is small.
proposed_fix: Add delivery_kind == 'free_hit' indicator to EV model with interaction on dismissal probability term. Set expected wicket contribution to 0 for free hits.

description: Super Over deliveries are excluded from elig_wp_training but their elig_pressure status was not independently verified in the audit. If Super Over deliveries have incorrect runs_required_before or target setup, their v_bat/v_bowl will be computed against wrong baselines. Super Overs also have unusual resource structures (6 balls, no powerplay restrictions) that the EV model was not trained to represent.
impact_on_rankings: UNVERIFIED: Cannot confirm Super Over exclusion coverage without additional audit run. If included with wrong context, a small number of deliveries may have anomalous v_bat/v_bowl values.
proposed_fix: Audit Super Over delivery count in pressure CSV. Confirm elig_pressure = 0 for Super Over deliveries or verify baseline computation is correct.

description: The IPL Impact Player substitution rule (allowing a tactical substitute mid-match) can cause a player to bat at an unexpected position. If the batting_order assignment in step1 uses innings position rather than a pre-match designation, Impact Player batters may be misclassified into wrong batting-role bins, which affects their role prior and shrinkage target.
impact_on_rankings: LOW-UNVERIFIED: Affects role-bin assignment for Impact Player batters. May cause minor misclassification of batting-role priors.
proposed_fix: Check whether any top-10 batter in the final rankings was used as an Impact Player and confirm their role bin is correct.

description: The validation simulation shows top-10 recovery rate of 22.7% — meaning in simulated datasets with the same true signal, only about 1 in 4 runs correctly identifies all 10 true top players. This is well below any useful prediction threshold and indicates the rankings have very low SNR.
impact_on_rankings: HIGH: The rankings cannot reliably distinguish 10 true top performers from a universe of eligible players given the observed sample sizes and noise levels. This should be prominently disclosed in any presentation or submission.
proposed_fix: Present rankings as 'best supported candidates given available data' not as definitive identifications. Report CI for each player. Recommend that the organiser treat the rankings as a probabilistic shortlist rather than a definitive ordered list.

description: The leverage computation classifies outcomes into 6 categories including 'two_three' with RUNS_BY['two_three'] = 2.5. Actual 2s and 3s have different win-probability impacts. By averaging them at 2.5 the leverage calculation introduces a small bias particularly in death-over situations where 3s are rarer but individually more impactful.
impact_on_rankings: LOW: Small number of 3s (rare in T20). Impact on leverage is marginal.
proposed_fix: Split 'two_three' into separate 'two' and 'three' categories with RUNS_BY values 2 and 3 respectively.

description: The dataset covers 2022 onwards — approximately 3-4 IPL seasons. Many players have limited samples because they are genuinely infrequently selected or were injured in some seasons. The model treats all seasons as homogeneous (no season or era effect). A player whose 2022 form was different from 2024 form is treated identically.
impact_on_rankings: MEDIUM: If player true ability has changed over time (improvement, decline, injury recovery) the pooled estimate is a mixture of different ability levels. For short-career players this is less problematic; for established veterans it may mask performance trends.
proposed_fix: Add recency weighting as a sensitivity check: apply 2x weight to 2024-25 deliveries vs 2022-23 deliveries. Report whether top-10 membership changes substantially.
